learning: Compare directly with iteration 1, which differs only by wheel_track (0.12 vs 0.10 m) and the kp scaling. If oval finishes hold near 0.7 and slalom line losses fall, yaw response was the limit. If oscillation rises above about 0.3 with finishes falling, the yaw gain is still too high, so reduce kp further or test mass 0.6 kg.
notes: Controller retuned for the shorter wheel_track: kp scaled from 5.0 to 4.5 to match the higher yaw gain, with kd 0.6 and base_speed 1.2 kept from the best raced design (iteration 1).
rationale: Iteration 1 is the best raced design (score 324.07). It gives oval finish rate 0.70 and s-bend and slalom progress of 0.38 and 0.12. Iteration 2 changed sensor_size and also base_speed (1.2 to 1.1) and kd (0.6 to 0.8), so the oval collapse cannot be attributed to the footprint alone. The Builder now proposes reverting sensor_size to 0.012 m and cutting wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, a 20% shorter track that gives about 20% more yaw rate per unit of wheel differential. To keep the effective steering loop close to the iteration 1 tuning, I scale kp by 0.10/0.12 (5.0 to 4.5). I keep kd at 0.6, the value that held oscillation near 0.26 on the oval, and base_speed at 1.2, which kept the oval completion time near 1.9 s. ki stays at 0.05 and line_loss stays at last_direction. Sensor weights stay [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1] to match the unchanged widened row. Expected result, not yet measured: oval finish rate near 0.7, max_error on s-bend and slalom closer to or below 0.06 m, and steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3. The main risk is that the yaw change still raises oscillation enough to cost oval finishes.
